questions.question: During rising from a chair, the muscles that provide the major extension torque are the:
questions.explanation: Trunk flexion forward shifts the centre of mass over the feet first.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During stair descent the quadriceps work mainly:
questions.explanation: Quadriceps weakness makes stairs difficult.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the late cocking phase of overhead throwing the shoulder is in:
questions.explanation: Rotator cuff and anterior capsule are loaded.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A push-up mainly uses the pectoralis major, triceps and:
questions.explanation: A plus at the top of the push-up trains serratus anterior.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A pull-up requires strong:

options.D: Latissimus dorsi, biceps and scapular depressors

questions.explanation: Closed kinetic chain of the upper limb.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During a squat, as the knee flexes the ankle:

options.C: Dorsiflexes and the hip flexes, with the trunk leaning forward to keep the centre of mass over the base

questions.explanation: Limited ankle dorsiflexion restricts squat depth.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Reaching the hand overhead requires:

options.B: Scapular upward rotation, glenohumeral flexion and thoracic extension

questions.explanation: Combined movement of the shoulder complex.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bringing the hand to the mouth uses mainly:

options.C: Elbow flexion with forearm supination and shoulder flexion

questions.explanation: Biceps brachii is a prime mover.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Placing the hand behind the back (combing the back) requires shoulder:
questions.explanation: Early loss in adhesive capsulitis.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At heel strike the gluteus maximus and hamstrings:

options.C: Contract to control hip flexion and decelerate the thigh

questions.explanation: Hip extensors work in late swing.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During running, the ground reaction force at foot strike is approximately:
questions.explanation: Higher than walking (1.2 times).
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which sequence of joint extension occurs during a vertical jump?

options.B: Hip, knee and ankle extension in proximal-to-distal sequence

questions.explanation: Triple extension.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Elbow flexor torque is greatest at about:
questions.explanation: Where the moment arm is longest.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During arm abduction the joint reaction force at the glenohumeral joint is mainly due to:

options.C: Muscle contraction rather than arm weight

questions.explanation: Rotator cuff muscles compress the humeral head.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In single-leg stance the abductor muscles must generate a force approximately equal to:
questions.explanation: Because of the short lever arm compared with the body weight lever.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The tibiofemoral compressive force during stair climbing is approximately:
questions.explanation: Walking about 2–3 times.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: As the knee flexes, the force of the quadriceps required to hold the position:

options.A: Increases because the moment arm of the body weight increases

questions.explanation: Wall sit endurance depends on this.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During late stance the ankle joint compressive force can reach:
questions.explanation: Achilles tendon forces reach several times body weight in running.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The compressive force on the L5–S1 disc when lifting a 20 kg weight with a flexed trunk may reach:

options.A: Several thousand newtons, many times body weight

questions.explanation: Moment arm and trunk flexion amplify the load.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Prolonged sitting in a slumped posture causes the lumbar spine to:

options.B: Flex, loading the posterior ligaments and discs

questions.explanation: Lumbar support restores the lordosis.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Lowering a weight slowly is an example of:
questions.explanation: The muscle lengthens while contracting.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Compared with concentric contraction, an eccentric contraction at the same speed can produce:
questions.explanation: Because cross-bridge detachment is slower and elastic elements contribute.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Muscle spindle stretch reflex latency in the quadriceps is approximately:
questions.explanation: Short because it is monosynaptic.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Electromechanical delay refers to:

options.B: The time lag between onset of EMG activity and force production

questions.explanation: About 30–100 ms.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The maximum force a muscle can generate is proportional to its:
questions.explanation: About 30–40 N per cm².
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The maximum excursion of a muscle depends mainly on its:
questions.explanation: Sartorius has long fibres and large excursion.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which muscle fibre type atrophies fastest with immobilisation?

options.B: Type I (slow-twitch), especially in antigravity muscles such as soleus

questions.explanation: Disuse favours loss of postural slow fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hypertrophy after resistance training is mainly due to:

options.C: Increased myofibrillar protein content in existing fibres

questions.explanation: Satellite cells assist.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After stopping training, muscle strength gains are:

options.D: Gradually lost within weeks to months

questions.explanation: Maintenance doses reduce loss.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Muscle tone at rest is the:

options.C: Resistance felt on passive stretch due to neural and viscoelastic factors

questions.explanation: Reduced in cerebellar lesions.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the ‘lower crossed syndrome’ of Janda the tight muscles are:
questions.explanation: Weak abdominals and gluteals.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In upper crossed syndrome the weak muscles include:

options.B: Deep neck flexors and lower trapezius/serratus anterior

questions.explanation: Tight pectorals and upper trapezius.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Tight hamstrings tend to produce:

options.A: Posterior pelvic tilt and flattening of the lumbar lordosis

questions.explanation: Seen in flat back posture.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Excessive subtalar pronation during stance is commonly associated with:

options.A: Medial rotation of the tibia and increased knee valgus

questions.explanation: Contributes to patellofemoral and shin pain.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Walking speed is the product of:
questions.explanation: Increased by lengthening step or raising cadence.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The swing phase of normal gait occupies approximately:
questions.explanation: Stance phase 60%.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At terminal stance (heel off) the muscle activity is mainly of the:
questions.explanation: Propulsion begins.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hip extension of about 10–20° occurs during walking at:
questions.explanation: Lack of hip extension shortens the step of the opposite limb.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which abdominal muscle is the main trunk rotator to the opposite side?

options.C: External oblique (opposite side) with contralateral internal oblique

questions.explanation: Right external oblique with left internal oblique rotates the trunk to the left.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Transversus abdominis contributes to spinal stability by:

options.D: Raising intra-abdominal pressure and tensioning the thoracolumbar fascia

questions.explanation: Feed-forward activation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The lumbar multifidus is important for:

options.A: Segmental stabilisation of the lumbar spine

questions.explanation: Atrophies in low back pain.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The quadratus lumborum acts as:

options.C: A lateral trunk flexor and hip hiker, stabilising the 12th rib

questions.explanation: Unilateral contraction laterally flexes the spine.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The iliopsoas muscle produces:

options.D: Hip flexion and, from a fixed femur, lumbar lordosis

questions.explanation: Femoral nerve and lumbar plexus supply.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Contraction of the diaphragm in quiet inspiration:

options.D: Descends the central tendon, increasing thoracic volume vertically and raising abdominal pressure

questions.explanation: Phrenic nerve C3–C5.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Supination of the forearm is performed by the:
questions.explanation: Biceps acts as a supinator when the elbow is flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Ulnar deviation of the wrist is performed by:

options.A: Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris

questions.explanation: Radial deviation: FCR, ECRL, ECRB, APL.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Opposition of the thumb is a combination of:

options.D: Abduction, flexion and medial rotation at the carpometacarpal joint

questions.explanation: Opponens pollicis is the prime mover.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Extension of the MCP joints of the fingers is performed by the:
questions.explanation: Lumbricals and interossei extend the IP joints.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The arches of the hand include the:

options.C: Proximal and distal transverse arches and longitudinal arches

questions.explanation: Maintained by ligaments and intrinsic muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Grip strength is usually measured with a:
questions.explanation: Jamar dynamometer; position 2 is standard.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Normal hip medial rotation range is approximately:
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation about 45°.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The knee joint can rotate only when it is:
questions.explanation: In extension the screw-home mechanism locks the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In full knee extension the patella is:

options.D: Mobile and free, lying proximal to the trochlear groove

questions.explanation: Quadriceps relaxation allows patellar mobility to be assessed.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Standing on tiptoes increases the height of the medial arch through the:
questions.explanation: Great toe extension tightens the plantar fascia.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The subtalar joint axis is oriented approximately:

options.D: 42° to the horizontal and 16° medial to the sagittal plane

questions.explanation: Produces triplanar pronation and supination.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)
